concept.title: Database configuration fields
concept.shortdesc: You must configure database connectivity for Red Hat Quay by setting the DB_URI field. You can optionally define connection settings such as SSL/TLS behavior by using DB_CONNECTION_ARGS.

section.title: Database URI
section.p: You configure the database connection for Red Hat Quay by setting the required DB_URI field.
The following table describes the DB_URI configuration field:

entry.p: The URI for accessing the database, including any credentials.

section.title: Database connection arguments
section.p: You can define optional connection arguments by using the DB_CONNECTION_ARGS parameter. Some of the key-value pairs under DB_CONNECTION_ARGS are generic, while others are database specific.

entry.p: Optional connection arguments for the database, such as timeouts and SSL/TLS.
Whether to use thread-local connections. Should always be True.
Whether to use auto-rollback connections. Should always be True.

section.codeblock: # ... DB_URI: postgresql://quayuser:quaypass@quay-server.example.com:5432/quay DB_CONNECTION_ARGS: autorollback: true threadlocals: true # ...

section.title: SSL/TLS connection arguments
section.p: With SSL/TLS, configuration depends on the database you are deploying.
The sslmode option determines whether Red Hat Quay negotiates a secure SSL/TLS TCP/IP connection with the server, and with what priority. The following modes are available:

entry.p: Determines whether, or with, what priority a secure SSL/TLS or TCP/IP connection is negotiated with the server.
Your configuration only tries non-SSL/TLS connections.
Your configuration first tries a non-SSL/TLS connection. Upon failure, tries an SSL/TLS connection.
Your configuration first tries an SSL/TLS connection. Upon failure, tries a non-SSL/TLS connection.
Your configuration only tries an SSL/TLS connection. If a root CA file is present, it verifies the certificate in the same way as if verify-ca was specified.
Your configuration only tries an SSL/TLS connection, and verifies that the server certificate is issued by a trusted certificate authority (CA).
Only tries an SSL/TLS connection, and verifies that the server certificate is issued by a trusted CA and that the requested server hostname matches that in the certificate.

section.p: For more information on the valid arguments for PostgreSQL, see Database Connection Control Functions in Additional resources.
